lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: why ads want us to want
lessonRef.focus: why ads want us to want

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 5 — money tools, privacy, and advertising
objective: Learners compute the real size of an advertised saving and test what happens to a pretend budget when an advertisement persuades a character to buy more than planned.
scenario: Tomas is a made-up third grader who sees an invented poster shouting that a toy usually priced at $5.00 is on sale for $3.00 today only. He has $5.00 of pretend money and did not plan to buy a toy at all.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compare the invented sale price with the invented regular price.

prompts.text: How much lower is the sale price than the regular price?

tasks.directions: The poster tells Tomas to grab two while the sale lasts. Work out what two would cost him, and compare that with the $5.00 he actually brought.

prompts.text: What would two sale toys cost Tomas?
How does that compare with the $5.00 Tomas has?

tasks.directions: Compare two endings: Tomas buys one sale toy, or Tomas walks past the poster and buys nothing.

prompts.text: How much would Tomas have left after buying one sale toy?
How much more would he have left by walking past instead?

tasks.directions: Tomas came in without a toy on his list.

prompts.text: The sale is real, and Tomas still might not want it. What is the ad trying to make him feel?

remediation: When a learner treats any discount as a reason to buy, cover the sale sign and ask what Tomas came in for, so the decision starts from his plan rather than from the poster.
extension: Have the learner rewrite the poster so it gives Tomas the same facts without the hurry, and explain what they removed.
